subject: ela
intro: When we read a story, we can ask questions to help us understand what is happening. Good readers ask WHO is in the story, WHAT happens, WHERE the story takes place, WHEN things happen, WHY characters do things, and HOW things happen. Asking and answering these questions helps us understand key details — the important facts the author wants us to know.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara loved going to the park on Saturday mornings. One day she saw a small dog sitting alone near the fountain. The dog looked cold and scared. Amara sat down slowly and held out her hand. The dog sniffed her fingers, then wagged its tail. "You need a friend today," Amara said softly.

WHO is the main character in this story?

steps: Ask yourself: who does the story talk about most?
The story begins with 'Amara loved going to the park,' so Amara is introduced first.
Every sentence in the story is about what Amara sees and does.
The dog is also in the story, but Amara is the one the story follows.
solution.answer: Amara is the main character. The story is about her visit to the park and what she does when she finds a lonely dog.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo's class was going on a field trip to the science museum on Friday. Leo woke up early and packed his notebook so he could draw pictures of the dinosaur bones. When the class arrived, the guide explained that the biggest dinosaur skeleton was a T. rex. Leo filled three pages with sketches before lunch.

WHEN did Leo's class go on the field trip?

steps: The question asks about time — look for words that tell 'when.'
The story says 'going on a field trip to the science museum on Friday.'
The word 'Friday' is the time clue that answers the question.
solution.answer: Leo's class went on the field trip on Friday.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia and her grandmother made tamales every winter. They stood side by side in the kitchen, spreading masa onto corn husks. Sofia's hands were small, so her tamales came out a little lumpy. "They taste just as good," her grandmother said with a smile. Sofia felt proud of every single one.

WHERE did Sofia and her grandmother make tamales?

steps: The question asks about place — look for words that describe a location.
The story says 'They stood side by side in the kitchen.'
'The kitchen' is the location word that answers the 'where' question.
solution.answer: Sofia and her grandmother made tamales in the kitchen.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

James could not find his backpack anywhere. He looked under his bed, behind the door, and in the closet. Finally he remembered — he had left it on the school bus yesterday. He called his mom, and she called the school. By afternoon, the bus driver had found the backpack safe and sound.

WHY could James not find his backpack at home?

steps: The question asks about a reason — look for an explanation of why something happened.
The story says James 'had left it on the school bus yesterday.'
That sentence explains the reason his backpack was missing from home.
solution.answer: James could not find his backpack because he had left it on the school bus the day before.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia had a loose tooth that had been wiggling for two weeks. She twisted it gently at breakfast and again at lunch. After school she bit into an apple, and out the tooth popped! She held it up and grinned a big, gap-toothed smile. Her dad took a picture to remember the moment.

HOW did Nadia's tooth finally come out?

steps: The question asks about how something happened — look for the action that caused the tooth to come out.
The story says 'After school she bit into an apple, and out the tooth popped!'
Biting into the apple is the action that made the tooth come out.
solution.answer: Nadia's tooth came out when she bit into an apple after school.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Owen woke up to the sound of rain tapping against his window. He had planned to ride his bike to the library, but the wet streets made that impossible. Instead, he grabbed his umbrella and walked. When he arrived, the librarian helped him find three books about ocean animals. Owen spent the whole afternoon reading at his favorite table by the window.

WHAT did Owen originally plan to do to get to the library?
items.hint: Look for the sentence that tells what Owen had planned before he saw the rain.

steps: The question asks 'what' — find the detail about Owen's original plan.
The story says 'He had planned to ride his bike to the library.'
'Ride his bike' is what he planned to do.
solution.answer: Owen originally planned to ride his bike to the library.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara's neighbor Mr. Chen had a garden full of tomatoes, sunflowers, and herbs. Every Tuesday he left a small basket of vegetables on his front steps for anyone who needed them. Amara always stopped to say thank you, even when Mr. Chen was not outside. One Tuesday she left a drawing of his garden in the basket as a gift.

WHEN did Mr. Chen leave vegetables on his steps?
items.hint: The story mentions a specific day of the week. Find that word.

steps: Look for a time word that tells 'when.'
The story says 'Every Tuesday he left a small basket of vegetables on his front steps.'
'Every Tuesday' answers the when question.
solution.answer: Mr. Chen left vegetables on his steps every Tuesday.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo loved playing soccer, but last spring he broke his arm and could not play for six weeks. His team kept practicing without him, and he felt left out. His coach invited him to sit on the bench and cheer. By the time Leo's arm healed, he had learned every player's position by watching so carefully.

WHY could Leo not play soccer for six weeks?
items.hint: Look for the sentence that tells what happened to Leo that stopped him from playing.

steps: The question asks for a reason — find the cause.
The story says 'last spring he broke his arm and could not play for six weeks.'
Breaking his arm is the reason he could not play.
solution.answer: Leo could not play soccer because he broke his arm.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia's family set up a lemonade stand at the end of their driveway on a hot July afternoon. Sofia made the lemonade by squeezing twelve lemons, adding cold water, and stirring in sugar until it dissolved. Her little brother James made a colorful sign. By five o'clock they had sold every cup and earned enough to buy supplies for next time.

HOW did Sofia make the lemonade?
items.hint: Look for the steps Sofia took — squeeze, add, stir. List them in order.

steps: The question asks 'how' — look for the steps or actions described.
The story says she made lemonade 'by squeezing twelve lemons, adding cold water, and stirring in sugar until it dissolved.'
List those three steps to answer the question.
solution.answer: Sofia made lemonade by squeezing twelve lemons, adding cold water, and stirring in sugar until it dissolved.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia's class put on a play about a brave explorer who sailed across a wide sea to find a hidden island. Nadia played the captain. She wore a big hat and a blue coat and spoke her lines in a loud, clear voice. After the show, her teacher said, "You were wonderful, Nadia. You never forgot a single word."

WHO said that Nadia was wonderful after the play?
items.hint: Find the sentence where someone speaks words of praise after the show.

steps: The question asks 'who' said something — find the speaker in the story.
The story says "her teacher said, 'You were wonderful, Nadia.'"
'Her teacher' is the person who spoke those words.
solution.answer: Nadia's teacher said she was wonderful after the play.
